name: Washburn Tunnel
facts: The Washburn Tunnel, completed in 1950, was the first toll‑free vehicular tunnel in the Southern United States, stretching 2,909 feet beneath the Houston Ship Channel for uninterrupted north‑south travel.

Engineered with a 6% roadway grade and three high‑speed Westinghouse Sturtevant blower fans, the tunnel exchanges its entire air volume every two minutes to keep carbon monoxide levels safe for drivers.

On March 1, 2020, operations of the Washburn Tunnel transferred to the Harris County Toll Road Authority, which plans extensive repairs and upgrades while keeping the tunnel toll‑free for all motorists.
